title: Counting pages from digits
prompt:
The page numbers of a ledger run 1, 2, 3 and so on, with nothing skipped. Printing all of them took 369 digit stamps.

How many pages are in the ledger?
hints: Do all page numbers use the same number of digits?
How many digits are used up by the pages with one-digit numbers, and then by the pages with two-digit numbers?
How many digits are left over for the longer numbers, and how many pages is that?
solution:
**159.**

First use up the short pages. Counting complete blocks: 1-digit pages (1 to 9): 9 pages × 1 = 9 digits; 2-digit pages (10 to 99): 90 pages × 2 = 180 digits. That is 189 digits.

That leaves 369 − 189 = 180 digits, all in 3-digit page numbers, so there are 180 ÷ 3 = 60 more pages after page 99. The last page is 99 + 60 = **159**.

The common slip is dividing 369 by 3 straight away. That treats every page as having a 3-digit number, including pages 1 to 9.
